primary_closest_work.title: From Fake to Real: Pretraining on Balanced Synthetic Images to Prevent Spurious Correlations in Image Recognition
primary_closest_work.supports: Under the paper's standard setting and source-distribution assumptions, synthetic balancing can retain joint bias with source identity. Separate-stage training is an existing remedy.
primary_closest_work.does_not_establish: A universal theorem for every conceivable augmentation or proof that our unrun paired-editor protocol is novel.

primary_closest_work.title: ForAug: Mitigating Biases in Image Classification via Controlled Image Compositions
primary_closest_work.supports: Existing foreground/background recomposition, strong-augmentation stacking including RandAugment, erosion/dilation, boundary smoothing and two infill-model comparisons.
primary_closest_work.does_not_establish: Box precision or classifier agreement certifies every edited label, or that a reserved-editor paired full-training effect contrast has already been fully ruled in or out.

primary_closest_work.title: Automated Background Swapping for Robustness against Spurious Backgrounds
primary_closest_work.supports: Empirical undercoverage of foreground labels harms the reported setup more than overcoverage; authors limit scope to background shortcuts.
primary_closest_work.does_not_establish: Their heavy-augmentation baseline is canonical full RandAugment, or auxiliary-mask noise equals group-proxy errors.

primary_closest_work.title: A Whac-A-Mole Dilemma: Shortcuts Come in Multiples Where Mitigating One Amplifies Others
primary_closest_work.supports: Multiple preexisting shortcuts can substitute for one another under mitigation.
primary_closest_work.does_not_establish: The exact causal policy effect for a newly proposed data route.

primary_closest_work.title: Leveraging Text-to-Image Generation for Handling Spurious Correlation
primary_closest_work.supports: Existing multiattribute synthetic balancing, including hair length and shape.
primary_closest_work.does_not_establish: Model-based pruning proves causal influence or edited-label truth.
